scope: Read-only source/doc reconciliation; no engine calculations, tests, provider calls or runtime health checks were executed. The report itself is the only written file.
markMeaning: One visual part represents a source module, calculation stage, data table, record or dependency. Geometry is an editorial explanation, not physical hardware or measured anatomy.

statusSemantics.implemented: The named source path performs the described operation; no claim of current deployment or empirical validity.
statusSemantics.simplified: The path exists but uses declared heuristics, approximate or partial logic; limitations remain visible.
statusSemantics.delegated: The operation requires an external provider, sidecar or database and may be disabled/unavailable.
statusSemantics.placeholder: The current path substitutes simulated or non-equivalent behavior for the described future capability.

engines.label: Panchanga
engines.summary: Five calendar limbs derived from the Sun, Moon and weekday.
engines.statusNote: Native computation exists; it uses an approximate fixed ayanamsa and a mean-longitude fallback. No sunrise-based location calculation is in this engine entry point.

reconciliations.claim: General docs describe date, latitude/longitude and timezone as the Panchanga calculation inputs.
reconciliations.truth: calculate() consumes date/time/timezone; latitude and longitude do not feed compute_panchanga. Timezone names are a limited static offset table, not full historical DST resolution.

reconciliations.claim: Astronomical precision may appear uniform across Vedic engines.
reconciliations.truth: Panchanga uses fixed 23.72 degrees and a mean-position fallback; Transits calculates Lahiri ayanamsa per datetime. Their precision paths are different.

parts.label: Sun & Moon
parts.description: Parses the selected date and time, obtains local Swiss Ephemeris tropical Sun/Moon longitudes, and falls back to mean-longitude formulas when that lookup fails.

parts.label: Sidereal offset
parts.description: Subtracts a fixed 23.72-degree Lahiri approximation from tropical longitude. This is an explicit approximation rather than an epoch-varying ayanamsa.

parts.label: Tithi
parts.description: Divides the angular separation of Moon and Sun into 30 twelve-degree lunar days, then resolves the Sanskrit name.

parts.label: Nakshatra
parts.description: Divides sidereal lunar longitude into 27 equal mansion segments and resolves the name from the local table.

parts.label: Yoga
parts.description: Adds sidereal Sun and Moon longitudes and divides their wrapped sum into 27 yoga segments.

parts.label: Karana
parts.description: Maps the half-tithi slot across the 60-slot month into seven repeating and four fixed karana identities.

parts.label: Vara
parts.description: Resolves weekday from Julian day into one of seven named varas. The displayed set belongs to one computed PanchangaResult.

engines.label: Vedic Clock
engines.summary: A local-hour lens joining the TCM organ clock, dosha cycles and optional calendar qualities.
engines.statusNote: The active entry point is a TCM-organ/dosha clock. Hora, Choghadiya and Vedic API helper modules exist but are not called by this calculate() path.

reconciliations.claim: The OpenAPI stub describes a muhurta/guna clock.
reconciliations.truth: build_result emits current_organ, current_dosha, recommendation, synthesis, timezone and upcoming_transitions. The engine is not the muhurta/guna schema.

reconciliations.claim: All integration modules in the crate look like active engine stages.
reconciliations.truth: engine.rs imports the organ/dosha and local recommendation modules; it does not invoke hora_integration, choghadiya_integration or panchang_integration.

reconciliations.claim: Timezone metadata describes support for IANA timezones generally.
reconciliations.truth: timezone_minutes_from_string recognizes Asia/Kolkata, Asia/Calcutta, UTC, GMT and explicit signed offsets. Other IANA names fall back to UTC in this entry point.

parts.label: Local clock
parts.description: Resolves offset minutes in priority order: options.timezone_offset, birth_data.timezone, then UTC. It records the selected source in the result.

parts.label: Organ windows
parts.description: Looks up one of twelve two-hour organ windows, carrying its associated element, emotion and activity text. These are traditional correspondences, not organ measurements.

parts.label: Dosha periods
parts.description: Maps local hour to the six daily dosha periods and their curated qualities. The same local hour drives both the organ and dosha layers.

parts.label: Calendar qualities
parts.description: When supplied, tithi and nakshatra indices select qualities that enrich temporal recommendations. This module consumes indices; it does not calculate their astronomy.

parts.label: Activity windows
parts.description: Combines organ/dosha affinities into ranked time windows for an optional requested activity, and checks whether that activity is favorable now.

parts.label: Upcoming transitions
parts.description: Scans future hours for organ or dosha changes and reports the next transitions. This is a clock schedule, not a physiological forecast.

parts.label: Temporal synthesis
parts.description: Builds the combined organ/dosha recommendation with optional calendar context; witness prompts adapt the language to the requested consciousness level.

engines.label: Vimshottari
engines.summary: A nested planetary-period clock seeded by sidereal natal Moon position.
engines.statusNote: The native path computes nested periods. Its constructor stores an HD engine but calculate() calls the shared ephemeris directly; timezone support and ayanamsa are simplified.

reconciliations.claim: The atlas names Human Design as a Vimshottari dependency.
reconciliations.truth: with_hd_engine stores a field marked allow(dead_code); calculate() creates EphemerisCalculator itself. This is constructor wiring, not a nested Human Design calculation.

reconciliations.claim: The full three-level timeline is implied to be returned in every response.
reconciliations.truth: serialize_timeline emits top-level mahadashas and antardasha_count; detailed three-level data is exposed only for current_period.

parts.label: Natal Moon
parts.description: Resolves birth time and asks the shared ephemeris for Moon longitude, then applies a fixed 23.72-degree sidereal offset. Alternatively accepts a supplied moon_longitude.

parts.label: Birth mansion
parts.description: Selects the birth nakshatra from lunar longitude and retrieves its ruling planet from the 27-mansion table.

parts.label: Dasha balance
parts.description: Measures progress through the birth mansion to calculate the remaining fraction of the first major period.

parts.label: Nine major periods
parts.description: Builds nine ordered planetary periods using their declared lengths and the remaining balance of the initial period.

parts.label: Nested periods
parts.description: Expands each major period into nine subperiods and each of those into nine further periods, giving 81 antardashas and 729 pratyantardashas.

parts.label: Present & thresholds
parts.description: Locates the three periods containing current_time and selects the next five transitions. Complete inner timelines exist in memory; the serializer summarizes major periods.

parts.label: Planetary qualities
parts.description: Combines the active lords’ curated themes, life areas, opportunities and challenges, then uses the active periods and transitions for witness questions.

engines.label: Transits
engines.summary: Two planetary reference planes compared through aspects, retrogrades and Saturn-cycle rules.
engines.statusNote: Astronomical positions are computed through Swiss Ephemeris. Aspect meanings and period quality are interpretive rules, not event predictions.

reconciliations.claim: TransitsResultSchema advertises dominant_transit, intensity and next_peak_date.
reconciliations.truth: The runtime serializer emits position arrays, aspects, sade_sati, period_quality and retrograde_planets; the stub fields are not produced.

parts.label: Natal sky
parts.description: Parses the birth datetime with chrono_tz and computes twelve natal sidereal positions, including Rahu and Ketu.

parts.label: Current sky
parts.description: Calculates the same twelve bodies at current_time, using date-specific Lahiri ayanamsa and signed longitudinal speed.

parts.label: Angular aspects
parts.description: Compares transit positions with natal positions, tests allowed aspect angles/orbs, determines applying/separating state, then filters significant aspects.

parts.label: Sade Sati
parts.description: Checks the transit Saturn sign against the natal Moon sign and labels rising, peak or setting when adjacent/sign conditions match.

parts.label: Retrograde motion
parts.description: A negative longitude speed marks retrograde motion; the engine collects these flags into a list for interpretation.

parts.label: Period quality
parts.description: Combines aspect nature, Sade Sati and retrograde flags into a qualitative period label and level-adapted witness questions.

engines.label: Biorhythm
engines.summary: Six date-seeded sine cycles, combined scores and an optional future sampling window.
engines.statusNote: This is a deterministic date-based model. None of the cycle names represent sensor measurements or established physiological predictions.

reconciliations.claim: docs/ENGINES.md lists three biological cycles.
reconciliations.truth: The runtime computes six named cycles plus three composites. The code consumes dates, not measured biology.

reconciliations.claim: The OpenAPI example uses flat signed scores.
reconciliations.truth: The runtime nests CycleResult objects with value in −1..1 and percentage in 0..100, plus phase and crossing metadata.

parts.label: Days since birth
parts.description: Parses birth and target dates, rejects a target before birth and uses the integer days-alive difference for every oscillator.

parts.label: Physical cycle
parts.description: Samples sin(2π × days_alive / 23), exposes both its signed value and its 0–100 mapped percentage.

parts.label: Emotional cycle
parts.description: Samples the same date formula with a 28-day period and attaches phase, next peak and next critical crossing.

parts.label: Intellectual cycle
parts.description: Samples the date formula with a 33-day period. It is a named model coordinate rather than measured cognitive performance.

parts.label: Extended cycles
parts.description: Computes intuitive, aesthetic and spiritual cycles using the same oscillator implementation and periods 38, 43 and 53 days.

parts.label: Composite rhythms
parts.description: Averages primary cycle percentages into mastery, passion and wisdom; overall_energy averages all six cycles.

parts.label: Crossings & forecast
parts.description: Finds upcoming zero-crossing days in the primary cycles and optionally samples all six cycles through a forecast window.

engines.label: Human Design
engines.summary: A BodyGraph assembled from two sets of thirteen planetary activations.
engines.statusNote: The chart generation and graph analysis are implemented. Its meaning is a traditional interpretive system; source execution does not establish physiological validity.

reconciliations.claim: chart.rs comments say centers, channels and derived properties are placeholders for a later agent.
reconciliations.truth: generate_hd_chart immediately calls analyze_hd_chart, which computes those fields. The introductory comment is stale.

reconciliations.claim: Some docs and renderers call the type field type or type_name.
reconciliations.truth: The actual serializer emits hd_type and eight named top-level keys. It does not serialize a separate strategy field.

parts.label: Birth-time resolver
parts.description: Parses the birth date, required birth time and IANA timezone, rejects ambiguous local time, and produces a UTC datetime.

parts.label: Design solar arc
parts.description: Searches backward for the moment when the Sun is 88 degrees before its birth longitude, providing the design-time reference.

parts.label: Twin activations
parts.description: Calculates thirteen personality and thirteen design planetary activations using the shared ephemeris, including Sun–Earth and lunar-node oppositions.

parts.label: Gate & line wheel
parts.description: Maps each longitude through the explicit Human Design gate sequence into one of 64 gates and one of six lines.

parts.label: Centers & channels
parts.description: Uses activated gate pairs to identify channels and define the nine centers; the graph is computed from both activation sets.

parts.label: Type & authority
parts.description: Derives type, authority, profile and connected-component definition from the completed graph and Sun activation lines.

parts.label: Witness lens
parts.description: Chooses level-adapted questions from the chart’s type, profile and authority. The response is rule-based local language.

engines.label: Gene Keys
engines.summary: Four Human Design gates expanded into an Activation Sequence and contemplative vocabulary.
engines.statusNote: This entry point is partial: four core activations only, each line fixed to 3. Venus and Pearl sequences are not calculated here. Frequency labels follow a supplied level, not a measured state.

reconciliations.claim: General engine docs advertise Activation, Venus, Pearl and Life’s Work as four sequences.
reconciliations.truth: Only ActivationSequence and four core activations are created by this entry point.

reconciliations.claim: active_keys.line looks like an astronomical calculation.
reconciliations.truth: create_chart_from_gates fixes every line to 3 on both input branches. This limitation is explicitly documented in the source.

parts.label: Gate source
parts.description: Accepts four explicit hd_gates, or invokes the injected Human Design engine when birth_data is present and extracts its Sun/Earth gates.

parts.label: Four activations
parts.description: Builds the four Personality/Design Sun/Earth activations. Every line is assigned3 because the current gate-only adapter discards the actual line.

parts.label: 64-key library
parts.description: Looks up each gate’s local Gene Key record, including name, Shadow, Gift, Siddhi and programming-partner material.

parts.label: Activation Sequence
parts.description: Organizes the four gates into the runtime’s Life’s Work, Evolution, Radiance and Purpose pairs. No Venus/Pearl sequence is emitted.

parts.label: Frequency lens
parts.description: Uses the supplied consciousness_level to suggest a Shadow/Gift/Siddhi orientation and associated inquiry. It does not assess a measured consciousness frequency.

parts.label: Witness questions
parts.description: Generates a local reflective question from the chart and requested level, alongside the enriched active_keys response.

engines.label: Numerology
engines.summary: Name and date arithmetic exposed as traceable reduction chains.
engines.statusNote: Both letter maps and the six returned number types are implemented. Names are processed as ASCII letters; this is symbolic arithmetic rather than personality measurement.

reconciliations.claim: Generic public descriptions list only the headline numerology numbers.
reconciliations.truth: NumerologyResult also exposes chaldean_name and per-number reduction chains; these are useful inspectable components that flat summary schemas omit.

parts.label: Letter maps
parts.description: Stores separate Pythagorean 1–9 and Chaldean 1–8 letter-to-number tables. Unsupported characters do not contribute to the sum.

parts.label: Reduction core
parts.description: Repeatedly sums digits while preserving master numbers 11, 22, 33, returning both the final value and the complete reduction chain.

parts.label: Birth-date numbers
parts.description: Reduces year, month and day for Life Path and the day alone for Birthday. Both preserve the reducer’s master-number rule.

parts.label: Expression
parts.description: Maps all name letters through the Pythagorean table, sums them and reduces the result.

parts.label: Soul Urge
parts.description: Filters the name to A/E/I/O/U before Pythagorean mapping and reduction; Y is not counted as a vowel in this implementation.

parts.label: Personality
parts.description: Filters to ASCII consonants, then maps and reduces them independently of the vowel channel.

parts.label: Chaldean name
parts.description: Runs the whole name through the Chaldean table and the shared reducer, exposing a parallel name-number result.

engines.label: Biofield
engines.summary: A symbolic field computed from planetary correspondences, with an explicitly separate mock branch.
engines.statusNote: Birth-data calculations now run, contradicting older always-mock docs. They derive numerical correspondences from astrology; they do not measure a human field. Capture-like options in this native engine still produce mock metrics.

reconciliations.claim: docs/engines/biofield.md says is_mock_data is always true and the Vedic path is not active.
reconciliations.truth: engine.rs:119 invokes VedicBiofieldAnalyzer when birth_data is supplied; vedic/mod.rs returns is_mock_data=false for that branch.

reconciliations.claim: Capture-shaped options can be mistaken for actual captured analysis.
reconciliations.truth: The native capture-shaped branch explicitly generates mock metrics. Actual saved capture lookup is the separate biofield-capture engine.

reconciliations.claim: The birth time is described as timezone-aware.
reconciliations.truth: vedic/mod.rs parse_birth_datetime attaches UTC directly to the supplied naive birth datetime and does not read birth_data.timezone.

reconciliations.claim: The Vedic label can imply a sidereal planetary calculation equivalent to Panchanga or Transits.
reconciliations.truth: vedic/planetary.rs uses the shared calculator’s tropical longitude directly for zodiac signs; it contains no sidereal conversion. This source path differs from the explicit conversions in Panchanga and Transits.

parts.label: Natal positions
parts.description: The Vedic path computes natal planetary positions through the shared ephemeris. This path is selected only when birth_data exists.

parts.label: Planetary strengths
parts.description: Combines planetary dignity, sign-based house proxies and aspects into declared strength scores for the correspondence model.

parts.label: Seven chakra correspondences
parts.description: Maps pairs of planets and their strengths/aspects to seven chakra activity and balance values. These values are constructed correspondences, not sensor readings.

parts.label: Field indices
parts.description: Computes named fractal-dimension, entropy, coherence, symmetry and vitality indices from positions and aspects. Their names do not make them optical or physiological measurements.

parts.label: Temporal modulation
parts.description: Uses current planetary positions, Moon transit, lunar phase and weekday to modify the symbolic base metrics, then recalculates vitality.

parts.label: Simulated fallback
parts.description: Without birth_data, uses a seed/user-based generator. Capture-like options also map mock values into an 11-field shape with consent/quality echoes; this is not the Python capture pipeline.

parts.label: Witness dyad
parts.description: Turns the calculated or simulated model into local reflective language and an Aletheios/Pichet dyad. This is not a live LLM or clinical assessment.

engines.label: Face Reading
engines.summary: A consent-gated landmark adapter plus deterministic fallback and traditional symbolic interpretation.
engines.statusNote: A real MediaPipe bridge exists, but landmark-derived proportions and heuristic symbolic interpretation must remain distinct. is_mock_data=false is also used for byte-seeded and birth-data heuristics.

reconciliations.claim: docs/engines/face-reading.md calls the engine a stub with no image processing.
reconciliations.truth: There is a consent-gated MediaPipe sidecar hook and real-landmark mapper in landmarks.rs. Availability of that service was not checked in this source-only pass.

reconciliations.claim: is_mock_data=false means the result came from real CV.
reconciliations.truth: heuristic_from_seed and graceful image/birth fallback paths also set false; backend and landmark summary distinguish the actual producer.

parts.label: Media & consent
parts.description: Reads image bytes/MIME and consent from options. Only granted consent permits the configured face CV service call.

parts.label: 468-landmark service
parts.description: Calls the Python face-mesh service and accepts only a real landmark response. Timeout, disabled service, missing consent or service fallback diverts to a deterministic heuristic.

parts.label: Proportion map
parts.description: Consumes landmark distances, symmetry and facial proportions. Regional landmark sets produce normalized scores used by the interpretive layer.

parts.label: Five-element lens
parts.description: Maps geometric ratios and regional scores into dosha, five-element and zone vocabulary. These symbolic mappings do not establish personality traits or medical conditions.

parts.label: Deterministic fallback
parts.description: When CV is unavailable, hashes image bytes or birth-data attributes into a seed and creates heuristic observations. This branch is not equivalent to landmark detection.

parts.label: Backend & quality
parts.description: Names mediapipe-face-cv, heuristic-image-landmark-hook, birth-physiognomy-fallback or mock-stub; carries quality/consent and optional landmark summary.

parts.label: Witness questions
parts.description: Generates level-adapted local questions from the analysis. The atlas should explain the code’s symbolic mapping without presenting its health or personality labels as established facts.

engines.label: NadaBrahman
engines.summary: A recommendation lattice selecting musical material by time, dosha and rasa.
engines.statusNote: The native engine recommends catalogued ragas and optional frequency correspondences. It does not ingest or analyze a voice recording, and it does not synthesize audio.

reconciliations.claim: docs/ENGINES.md describes audio_data, vocal-pattern analysis and frequency signatures.
reconciliations.truth: analyze() reads current_time plus optional dosha/rasa/mood/chakra; no audio input is decoded or analyzed.

reconciliations.claim: NadaBrahman and Raaga can appear interchangeable.
reconciliations.truth: NadaBrahman recommends ragas; the TypeScript raaga engine resolves Melakarta ratios and can optionally create clips. They are separate engine identities.

parts.label: Prahar clock
parts.description: Maps input.current_time.hour() into one of eight three-hour prahars. The current implementation uses the supplied UTC clock hour directly.

parts.label: Time-based ragas
parts.description: Looks up the prahar’s ragas and their declared scores, choosing a primary and secondary set; a universal-raga fallback exists if the list is empty.

parts.label: Dosha affinity
parts.description: Adds recommendations from the supplied dosha name’s curated affinity list. The engine does not derive the user’s dosha.

parts.label: Rasa & mood
parts.description: Adds recommendations from the provided rasa or mood. These are curated associations rather than measured emotional-state inference.

parts.label: Recommendation weave
parts.description: Deduplicates by raga number, retains higher scores, combines reasons when replacing an entry, sorts descending and returns the top five.

parts.label: Chakra frequency map
parts.description: Resolves supplied chakra names into declared solfeggio and binaural-target frequencies. No acoustic analysis or physiological measurement occurs.

parts.label: Musical inquiry
parts.description: Builds local time/raga/dosha-oriented questions and enriches recommendations with arohanam, avarohanam and catalogued qualities.

engines.label: Tarot
engines.summary: A seeded deck draw assembled into positions, orientations and local symbolic readings.
engines.statusNote: The deck/spread reading path is implemented. Interpretations are local text. The provenance confidence value 1 describes this deterministic source path, not divinatory accuracy.

reconciliations.claim: docs/ENGINES.md describes birth cards, yearly cards and life-path card sequences.
reconciliations.truth: This engine entry point performs named spread readings. It does not calculate birth-card or year-card numerology.

reconciliations.claim: The OpenAPI stub describes focal_card and synthesis.
reconciliations.truth: The actual result contains spread, question, positions and seed; focal_card/synthesis are not produced here.

parts.label: 78-card library
parts.description: Loads the 22 Major Arcana and 56 generated Minor Arcana records, with suit, element, keywords and upright/reversed meanings.

parts.label: Spread architecture
parts.description: Resolves one of five spreads and its ordered positions, each with its own meaning and required card count.

parts.label: Seeded shuffle
parts.description: Inside drawCards, SeededRandom shuffles a copy of the full deck before selection, so the same seed reproduces the card order.

parts.label: Draw & orientation
parts.description: Draws the requested number of cards from the shuffled deck and assigns upright/reversed orientations using the seeded random stream.

parts.label: Position readings
parts.description: Pairs each drawn card with a spread position, selecting the upright or reversed meaning while carrying the card keywords.

parts.label: Question lens
parts.description: Builds seed-aware witness questions from the finished reading. calculate() also records deterministic local provenance, with no generated-text fallback.

engines.label: I Ching
engines.summary: A seeded consultation scaffold around a 64-hexagram text library.
engines.statusNote: The current casting and relating-hexagram calculation are simplified placeholders. Do not present this as an exact three-coin or yarrow procedure.

reconciliations.claim: Metadata advertises three_coins and yarrow_stalks casting methods.
reconciliations.truth: method is only echoed in the result; both labels execute the same uniform 6–9 sampler.

reconciliations.claim: The relating hexagram is the primary transformed by its changing lines.
reconciliations.truth: The flipped relatingLines array is unused; another rng.nextInt(1,64) supplies the relating hexagram.

parts.label: 64-hexagram library
parts.description: Provides six-line patterns and curated judgment/image/name records for the selected hexagram number.

parts.label: Primary selection
parts.description: Uses a validated explicit hexagram 1–64 or chooses a random number uniformly. The primary is chosen independently of the six cast line values.

parts.label: Six sampled lines
parts.description: Samples each line uniformly from 6, 7, 8, 9. This makes the changing-line probability 50%, and the method parameter does not alter the sampling.

parts.label: Changing-line mask
parts.description: Marks positions with sampled value 6 or 9 as changing. The primary’s lines are flipped in a local array, but that array is not used to select the relating hexagram.

parts.label: Relating placeholder
parts.description: When any line changes, selects another random hexagram number instead of resolving the flipped six-line pattern. This is an acknowledged source stub, not a valid transformation.

parts.label: Consultation questions
parts.description: Builds reflective prompts from the selected primary/relating records and changing positions, then returns the method label and line samples.

engines.label: Enneagram
engines.summary: A questionnaire or type lookup joined to nine-pattern taxonomy and reflective movement.
engines.statusNote: The questionnaire scoring and lookup paths exist. Confidence is a score-gap heuristic, not a calibrated psychological probability; birth data does not determine the type.

reconciliations.claim: docs/ENGINES.md lists date/name input and instinctual stacking.
reconciliations.truth: calculate() consumes answers or explicit type/wing; it does not derive a type from date/name and does not emit instinctual stacking.

reconciliations.claim: The model’s confidence can be read as validated psychological certainty.
reconciliations.truth: The value is a declared gap-of-scores formula, not a calibrated likelihood or clinical result.

parts.label: 45-question bank
parts.description: Defines 45 weighted statements tied to types and can return them without performing an assessment.

parts.label: Nine score channels
parts.description: Accumulates answer×weight by associated type, normalizes against each type’s maximum and sorts the nine scores.

parts.label: Primary & wing
parts.description: Chooses the highest score as primary and the highest-scoring adjacent type as wing; direct lookup instead validates a supplied type and adjacent wing.

parts.label: Confidence & tritype
parts.description: Confidence is min(1, gap between top two normalized scores /30). A tritype is included only at confidence ≥ 0.3.

parts.label: Movement & centers
parts.description: Looks up integration/disintegration connections, center, Hornevian group, harmonic group and healthy/average/unhealthy trait text.

parts.label: Witness prompts
parts.description: Generates questions for assessment, type lookup or movement. With no parameters it returns starting guidance rather than an invented type.

engines.label: Sacred Geometry
engines.summary: A form-library browser with symbolism, meditation and an optional SVG-status check.
engines.statusNote: The TypeScript producer is real, but it returns curated form information rather than a procedural geometric mesh or vector-path construction. Atlas geometry is an explanatory representation.

reconciliations.claim: docs/ENGINES.md says the engine generates constructions and calculates proportions.
reconciliations.truth: The producer returns catalogue data and SVG validation status; it does not generate vertices, SVG d strings or proportional geometry.

reconciliations.claim: The OpenAPI stub includes point_count and symbolic_theme.
reconciliations.truth: Neither field is emitted. form.numerology is a symbolic catalog number, and must not be substituted for a calculated point count.

parts.label: Form library
parts.description: Stores the named sacred forms and their descriptions, symbolism, elements, numerology and meditation prompts.

parts.label: Form selection
parts.description: Validates an explicit hyphenated form ID or uses SeededRandom to pick a catalogue entry. It does not generate a new shape.

parts.label: Symbolic anatomy
parts.description: Projects the selected form’s name, description, elements, numerology and symbolism into the result. Numerology is a per-form symbolic constant, not a mesh point count.

parts.label: Meditation layer
parts.description: Returns the form’s stored meditation prompt and a fixed 5–15 minute duration suggestion, carrying the optional intention.

parts.label: SVG status
parts.description: Checks whether supplied markup resembles a complete SVG and lacks two simple script patterns; returns status/reason only. It neither returns SVG markup nor supplies a complete sanitizer.

parts.label: Witness lens
parts.description: Selects form/intention-aware questions using the seed. Geometric forms in the atlas should be labelled conceptual visualizations of this catalog.

engines.label: Sigil Forge
engines.summary: Intention reduction and ritual guidance with an optional external image-generation branch.
engines.statusNote: Four guidance methods exist; only word elimination computes a letter sequence. Image generation/editing is provider-configured and optional. The engine does not generate a deterministic vector glyph.

reconciliations.claim: OpenAPI describes sigil_id and vector_path, and general docs list planetary/angelic methods.
reconciliations.truth: The current producer has four guidance methods and no vector-path generator. Only word-elimination derives letters; imagery is optional provider output.

reconciliations.claim: Older per-engine docs describe NVIDIA NIM as the only image path.
reconciliations.truth: The engine now uses an ImageProvider abstraction with default/configured providers and optional edit support.

reconciliations.claim: A requested image flag guarantees an image is included.
reconciliations.truth: guidance.note currently keys on the request flag even if the provider returns an error. A viewer must use generated_image content/status, not this optimistic sentence.

parts.label: Intention
parts.description: Accepts question or intention/intent/intent_text aliases, requires nonempty text and trims it before method selection.

parts.label: Method library
parts.description: Resolves word-elimination, rose-wheel, pictographic or chaos-star. Automatic choice uses intention length/word count or a seeded pick.

parts.label: Letter reduction
parts.description: Removes vowels and spaces, keeps each ASCII consonant once and returns uppercase remaining letters. Other methods return guidance without an equivalent geometric encoder.

parts.label: Charging suggestions
parts.description: Samples two charging methods and exposes method steps and witness prompts. These are symbolic practice instructions, not evidence of causal manifestation.

parts.label: Image prompt
parts.description: Builds a method/style/intention-specific text prompt, with optional reduced-letter hints. It describes an image; it does not compute a glyph path.

parts.label: Image provider
parts.description: Only requested image generation or editing calls the configured provider. Results carry image content or URL and metadata; unavailable providers and failures produce explicit errors.

parts.label: Guidance & media
parts.description: Returns guidance, processing, charging suggestions, optional generated_image and SVG status. The SVG check returns status only; no vector_path is emitted.

engines.label: Raaga
engines.summary: A 72-Melakarta musical catalog expanded into swaras, ratios and optional audio.
engines.statusNote: Full 72-entry construction and ratio output exist. Local clips are simple sine-note demonstrations; audio timbre/gamaka are explicitly deferred. Clip generation defaults off.

reconciliations.claim: docs/ENGINES.md calls this generative Hindustani composition.
reconciliations.truth: The active TypeScript producer is a Carnatic Melakarta ratio system. Local clip generation plays simple sine notes; it does not implement expressive composition/gamaka.

reconciliations.claim: audio_ref input suggests analysis of an existing audio recording.
reconciliations.truth: audio_ref is read but is not used to extract audio features or determine the raga in calculate().

reconciliations.claim: Seeded input/current_time implies all auto-selection is replayable.
reconciliations.truth: The current implementation uses new Date().getHours() for automatic selection/context, not input.current_time or the supplied seed.

parts.label: 72-Melakarta lattice
parts.description: Constructs the 72 Melakarta records with swara/shruti indices, arohana/avarohana arrays, names and ratios.

parts.label: Raga selector
parts.description: Resolves a name first, then number, otherwise dosha×prahar intersection or the first prahar recommendation. Automatic selection reads the server-local current hour.

parts.label: Swara frequencies
parts.description: Annotates eight ascending swaras with shruti index, rational and decimal ratio, then multiplies each by root_hz to obtain an annotated frequency.

parts.label: Prahar & dosha
parts.description: Reports whether the selected Melakarta is recommended for the current prahar, its dosha affinities and optional alternate ragas.

parts.label: Ratio interface
parts.description: Exposes strudel_ratios, root_hz and the ascending/descending index arrays for a consuming player; returning these arrays alone does not mean audio was rendered.

parts.label: Optional clip path
parts.description: request_clip plus granted consent enables mode local or service. Local mode synthesizes PCM16 mono sine notes with fades; service mode delegates rendering. Off/error paths retain null clip_url and a status.

parts.label: Musical inquiry
parts.description: Produces local Melakarta/dosha-aware questions beside the musical data and clip outcome metadata.

engines.label: Financial Biosensor
engines.summary: A declared decision-reflection composite over five engines and one optional biometric sample.
engines.statusNote: A composed reflection surface, not financial forecasting or a trading signal. Its house weights are unfitted; absence, coverage and insufficiency are explicit.

reconciliations.claim: Financial Biosensor can appear to be another standalone tradition engine or market predictor.
reconciliations.truth: The baseline calls it a composed-surface; source Declaration explicitly frames decision reflection and rejects forecasting. Its inputs contain no market-price feed.

reconciliations.claim: The engine comment says passing HD gates avoids Gene Keys’ second ephemeris pass.
reconciliations.truth: The copied Gene Keys input retains birth_data; GeneKeysEngine prioritizes birth_data over hd_gates, so this intended shortcut is not effective on that branch.

parts.label: Optional HRV sample
parts.description: Validates an optional time-stamped HRV sample and its freshness/range before spending work on the source engines. Missing HRV stays an absence.

parts.label: Five source engines
parts.description: Reads Human Design first, then Gene Keys, Vimshottari, Transits and Biorhythm. A failed source becomes an absence rather than a fabricated result.

parts.label: Six contributors
parts.description: Converts HRV and the five source results into chronofield, planetary weather, three-wave cycle, energetic-authority and gift/shadow scores with consumed-field provenance.

parts.label: Declared composite
parts.description: Renormalizes declared house weights over available contributors. Below 40% coverage it withholds the numeric value; missing HRV also lowers reported confidence.

parts.label: Temporal landscape
parts.description: Builds weekly/monthly reflection views using date-varying Biorhythm and Vimshottari information, keeping absent sources absent. These are model projections, not market forecasts.

parts.label: Decision ownership
parts.description: Reports which sources were present and absent, carries optional decision context, and asks questions that preserve the person’s ownership of the decision.

parts.label: Formula provenance
parts.description: Records formula version, contributor source/version, raw values, normalization, declared/effective weight, status, coverage and biometric factor.

engines.label: Biofield Capture
engines.summary: An owner-scoped resolver for a previously persisted capture analysis.
engines.statusNote: This engine does not take a photograph or run CV. It re-exposes an existing database reading; API registration requires an available Postgres pool.

reconciliations.claim: The name suggests this engine directly captures images or executes the Python CV service.
reconciliations.truth: Its calculate() only resolves a persisted reading. Image acquisition, CV and persistence occur upstream in the capture lifecycle.

reconciliations.claim: Nineteen declared engine identities implies every startup exposes all 19.
reconciliations.truth: noesis-api registers BiofieldCaptureEngine only when a database pool is available. Runtime availability cannot be inferred from the static catalog.

parts.label: Capture reference
parts.description: Requires options.biofield_capture.reading_id and parses it as a UUID. It addresses one persisted reading rather than accepting image pixels.

parts.label: Authenticated owner
parts.description: Requires the internal _auth.user_id UUID supplied by the authenticated API path. A reading ID alone is insufficient.

parts.label: Reading repository
parts.description: Calls ReadingsRepository.get_reading(reading_id,user_id) through the configured Postgres pool. Missing, foreign or unreachable data returns an error.

parts.label: Engine identity
parts.description: Rejects any retrieved record whose engine_id is not biofield-capture, preserving the distinction from natal Biofield readings.

parts.label: Captured analysis
parts.description: Carries the stored input/analysis, session ID, analysis version, contract version and quality_assessment into an EngineOutput. No new metrics are computed here.

parts.label: Capture reflection
parts.description: Reuses a nonempty stored witness prompt; otherwise asks a local question based on sufficient_quality and analysis_version.

topologySemantics: Connections express the described data dependency, shared rule or explicit alternative branch. Component geometry aggregates related source operations and does not represent runtime timing, traffic or physical engine hardware.
